name: Kuah pliek u
note: An Acehnese vegetable curry seasoned with fermented coconut residue.

name: Nasi jinggo
note: Small banana-leaf rice parcels contain modest portions of assorted side dishes.

name: Musik dambus
note: Bangka’s dambus is a string instrument with a carved deer-head-shaped neck.

name: Tari Andun
note: This southern Bengkulu social dance forms part of wedding celebrations.

name: Rampak bedug
note: Banten performers combine coordinated bedug drumming with choreographed movement.

name: Sulaman Karawo
note: Gorontalo artisans cut and withdraw fabric threads before embroidering openwork patterns.

name: Tari Rentak Kudo
note: This Kerinci dance from Hamparan Rawang is known for its stamping steps.

name: Pesa’an Madura
note: Madura’s men’s outfit includes loose trousers and a red-and-white striped shirt.

name: Roti buaya
note: Crocodile-shaped bread presented at Betawi weddings as a symbol of fidelity.

name: Baju Kurong
note: This Malay women’s ensemble is worn at weddings and traditional functions in West Kalimantan.

name: Busana adat Kustim
note: This Kutai Kartanegara court attire was traditionally reserved for royalty at important ceremonies.

name: Kebaya labuh
note: In Lingga, this long, front-opening kebaya is worn in traditional and ceremonial settings.

name: Baamar galung pancar matahari
note: This Banjar wedding ensemble combines sparkling decoration, golden accessories and floral adornments.

name: Baju Upak Nyamu
note: Nyamu bark is made into a plain sleeveless vest, simpler than the ornamented Sangkarut.

name: Busana adat Tidung: Selampoy
note: Selampoy is customary attire of the Tidung Ulun Pagun community associated with Tarakan.

name: Kerajinan manik-manik Dayak
note: Dayak artisans make patterned beadwork, one of North Kalimantan’s recognised local crafts.

name: Tari Cangget
note: Cangget forms part of begawi customary celebrations among Lampung Pepadun communities.

name: Tari lenso
note: Handkerchiefs animate this social dance performed at celebrations in Maluku.

name: Tari lalayon
note: Pairs exchange expressive gestures while waving white handkerchiefs.

name: Tenun Sukarara
note: Sukarara in Central Lombok is a center of traditional Sasak handweaving.

name: Pasola Sumba
note: In Sumba’s Pasola ritual, opposing groups of riders throw wooden spears from horseback.

name: Pembuatan noken pegunungan
note: Knotted or woven noken bags are part of daily life in Wamena and a wider Papuan craft tradition.

name: Tata kelola adat Egek Moi
note: In Malaumkarta, Moi communities temporarily close fishing areas so marine resources can recover.

name: Anyaman tas Kamoro
note: Kamoro women weave bags from local grasses, a craft also presented at cultural festivals.

name: Pacu jalur
note: Teams race long wooden boats in Kuantan Singingi’s traditional rowing competition.

name: Maengket
note: Minahasan performers combine group dance with singing in Maengket.

name: Randai
note: This Minangkabau theater combines storytelling, music, movement, and martial-arts elements.

name: Tari Lulo (Tolaki)
note: A communal dance associated with Tolaki communities.

name: Tari Pakarena (Makassar)
note: A South Sulawesi dance known for graceful movements and fan gestures.

name: Golla kambu
note: A Mandar sweet made with sticky rice, coconut and palm sugar.

name: Mie celor
note: Palembang-style noodles come with a thick coconut-milk and shrimp broth.

name: Uta dada
note: Smoked chicken or fish is cooked in a spiced coconut-milk broth.

name: Naniura
note: This Batak dish marinates raw fish in citrus juice and spices rather than cooking it over fire.
